label: Can delete animation set
summary: Whether the animation set selected in the GUI animation editor can be deleted.
details: It turns on the delete button of the animation sets list.

label: Can delete animations
summary: Whether the animations selected in the GUI animation editor can be deleted.
details: It turns on the delete button of the animations list.

label: Can rename animation set
summary: Whether the animation set selected in the GUI animation editor can be renamed.
details: It turns on the rename button of the animation sets list.

label: Can rename animation
summary: Whether the animation selected in the GUI animation editor can be renamed.
details: It turns on the rename button of the animations list.

label: Change set parent
summary: Changes which animation set the selected animation set inherits its animations from.
details: Its button in the GUI animation editor has this as its tooltip. A set inherits the animations of its parent set. It returns nothing.

label: Create animation set
summary: Creates a new animation set in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the new button of the animation sets list. It returns nothing.

label: Create animation
summary: Creates a new animation in the animation set selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the new button of the animations list. It returns nothing.

label: Delete animation set
summary: Deletes the animation set selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the delete button of the animation sets list. It returns nothing.

label: Delete animations
summary: Deletes the animations selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the delete button of the animations list. It returns nothing.

label: Delete keyframes
summary: Deletes all selected keyframes in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is a toolbar button above the tracks, which is on only while some keyframe is selected. It returns nothing.

label: Animation sets
summary: The list of animation sets known to the animation editor.
details: Going by its name. The game does not name its return type. It belongs to the game's internal animation editor, and no game file uses it.

label: Animations
summary: The list of animations shown in the animation editor.
details: Going by its name. The game does not name its return type. It belongs to the game's internal animation editor, and no game file uses it.

label: Available tracks
summary: The list of tracks that can be added in the animation editor.
details: Going by its name. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it.

label: Universal tracks
summary: The list of universal tracks of the animation editor's timeline.
details: Going by its name. The game does not name its return type. The same editor has a "universal track" type, so these are probably its items. No game file uses it.

label: Curve editor open
summary: Whether the GUI animation curve editor is open.
details: It marks the "Curve Editor" button of the GUI animation editor as pressed; that button opens the curve editor.

label: Can pick curve preset
summary: Whether the selected keyframes allow choosing a curve preset in the GUI animation editor.
details: While true the editor shows its list of preset curves; otherwise it shows a greyed-out note asking to select pairs of keyframes first.

label: Save
summary: Saves the changes made in the GUI animation editor back to the GUI animation files.
details: Its one use is the editor's save button, whose tooltip says so. It returns nothing.

label: Save as
summary: Opens a save dialog of the GUI animation editor to pick which animation files are saved, and where.
details: Its one use is the editor's save as button. It returns nothing.

label: Rename animation set
summary: Renames the animation set selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the rename button of the animation sets list. That button's tooltip speaks of the selected animation, the same text as the animations list's button. It returns nothing.

label: Rename animation
summary: Renames the animation selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the rename button of the animations list. It returns nothing.

label: Self
summary: The animation editor object itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. Here no game file uses it on the animation editor.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this animation set entry itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Animation set name
summary: The name shown for an animation set in the GUI animation editor's list.
details: It is the text of the set's entry in the "Animation Sets:" list.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether an animation set is selected in the GUI animation editor's list.
details: It shows the set's entry as pressed; clicking the entry switches it.

label: Self
summary: This animation set entry itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Toggle selected
summary: Selects an animation set in the GUI animation editor's list, or deselects it.
details: The set's entry calls it when clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this animation entry itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Animation name
summary: The name shown for an animation in the GUI animation editor's list.
details: It is the text of the animation's entry in the "Animations:" list.

label: Animation tooltip
summary: The tooltip text shown for an animation in the GUI animation editor's list.
details: Its one use is the tooltip of the animation's entry. What the text says is not shown.

label: Is inherited
summary: Whether an animation in the GUI animation editor's list comes from the parent set of the selected animation set.
details: While true, the entry shows a paste button that copies the animation into the selected set.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether an animation is selected in the GUI animation editor's list.
details: It shows the animation's entry as pressed; clicking the entry switches it. The tracks of the selected animations are shown on the right.

label: Copy inherited animation
summary: Copies an inherited animation from the set it comes from into the selected animation set.
details: Its button in the GUI animation editor has this as its tooltip and is shown only on inherited animations. The copy can then be changed in the selected set. It returns nothing.

label: Self
summary: This animation entry itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Toggle selected
summary: Selects an animation in the GUI animation editor's list, or deselects it.
details: The animation's entry calls it when clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this available track itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Add track
summary: Adds this track to the animation being edited in the GUI animation editor.
details: The track's entry in the add track dialog calls it when clicked, and the dialog closes. The entry cannot be clicked while the track is excluded. It returns nothing.

label: Track description
summary: The description of a track offered in the GUI animation editor's add track dialog.
details: The dialog shows it as the entry's tooltip and, while the track can be added, as a line under its name. The game does not register its return type.

label: Track name
summary: The name of a track offered in the GUI animation editor's add track dialog.
details: It is the text of the track's entry. The game does not register its return type.

label: Blocking track name
summary: The name of the already added track that keeps this track from being added.
details: The add track dialog of the GUI animation editor writes "Unavailable because [name] track is already added." on an excluded track. The game does not register its return type.

label: Is excluded
summary: Whether a track cannot be added because a track it conflicts with is already on the animation.
details: In the GUI animation editor's add track dialog an excluded track cannot be clicked and shows which added track blocks it instead of its description.

label: Self
summary: This available track itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this keyframe itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Keyframe position
summary: Where a keyframe's marker sits on its track in the GUI animation editor, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: Its one use places the keyframe marker on the track's timeline.

label: Keyframe time
summary: The time of a keyframe on the animation's timeline, in seconds, as a decimal number.
details: The GUI animation editor shows it with two decimals and an "s" next to the keyframe while the mouse is over it or it is dragged, unless the time is 0.

label: Has first keyframe switch
summary: Whether a keyframe carries the switch for where the animation takes its starting value.
details: The GUI animation editor puts an invisible button on the keyframe while this is true; its tooltip calls it the first keyframe's behaviour. The keyframe marker then shows one of two arrow pictures.

label: Value from widget
summary: Going by its name and its use, whether the first keyframe takes its value from the widget's state when the animation starts, rather than from the keyframe.
details: The GUI animation editor uses it to pick which of the two arrow pictures the first keyframe shows; the switch's tooltip says the down arrow means the value comes from the keyframe and the up arrow from the widget. Which picture belongs to true is not shown.

label: Is dragged
summary: Whether a keyframe is being dragged with the mouse in the GUI animation editor.
details: While true, as while the mouse is over it, the editor shows the keyframe's time next to it.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether a keyframe is selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: A selected keyframe is drawn in yellow, unless the mouse is over it, which draws it in blue.

label: Is under mouse
summary: Whether the mouse pointer is over a keyframe in the GUI animation editor.
details: The keyframe is then drawn in blue and its time is shown next to it.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether a keyframe is valid.
details: The GUI animation editor shows a keyframe's marker only while this is true. What makes a keyframe invalid is not shown.

label: Self
summary: This keyframe itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Switch starting value
summary: Switches where the animation takes its starting value: from the first keyframe, or from the widget's state when the animation starts.
details: The GUI animation editor's switch on the first keyframe calls it. Its tooltip says taking the value from the widget gives a smooth transition. It returns nothing.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the animation editor's metadata context itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Deselect all keyframes
summary: Clears the keyframe selection in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its button is on only while some keyframe is selected; its tooltip adds that a click anywhere on the tracks also deselects. It returns nothing.

label: Has selected keyframes
summary: Whether at least one keyframe is selected in the GUI animation editor.
details: It turns on the buttons that delete the selected keyframes and that deselect them all.

label: Animation lists hidden
summary: Whether the left panel of the GUI animation editor, with the animation set and animation lists, is folded away.
details: While true the panel is hidden and its collapse button shows as pressed.

label: Keyframe snapping on
summary: Whether keyframes snap into place when dragged along the timeline of the GUI animation editor.
details: It shows the snapping button as pressed. What they snap to is not shown.

label: Select all keyframes
summary: Selects every keyframe in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is a toolbar button above the tracks. It returns nothing.

label: Editor state
summary: The GUI animation editor's shared state itself, to hand to another function.
details: Its one use passes it to a curve editor control point's IsSelected, which checks the selection against it. The game does not register its return type.

label: Toggle animation lists
summary: Folds away the left panel of the GUI animation editor, with the animation set and animation lists, or opens it again.
details: The panel's collapse button calls it. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle keyframe snapping
summary: Switches the snapping of keyframes dragged on the timeline on or off.
details: Its button in the GUI animation editor has this as its tooltip. It returns nothing.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the animation editor's player itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Can play
summary: Whether the GUI animation editor's playback controls can be used.
details: It turns the whole row of playback buttons (loop, rewind, step, play, speed) on or off.

label: Selected playback speed
summary: Which playback speed is currently picked in the GUI animation editor's speed dropdown.
details: Its one use is as the selected entry of that dropdown. The game types it as a pair of whole numbers.

label: Current time
summary: The current playback time of the animation in the editor.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number, probably in seconds like the keyframe times, but the game does not say. No game file uses it.

label: Animation end
summary: The time at which the animation in the GUI animation editor ends, as a decimal number.
details: Its one use is the roll forward button, which moves the playback time to this value.

label: Speed multiplier
summary: The playback speed factor currently set in the animation editor.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The neighbouring SetSpeedMultiplier sets it. No game file uses it.

label: Playback speed
summary: The playback speeds offered in the GUI animation editor's speed dropdown.
details: Its one use fills that dropdown; each entry shows its own text. The game does not register its return type.

label: Is dragging time
summary: Whether the playback time marker is being dragged with the mouse.
details: Going by its name. It returns yes or no. No game file uses it.

label: Loop on
summary: Whether the GUI animation editor plays the animation in a loop.
details: It shows the loop button as pressed.

label: Is playing
summary: Whether the animation in the GUI animation editor is playing right now.
details: While it plays, the play button shows a pause picture and the step buttons are off; editing a track's properties is off too.

label: Self
summary: The animation editor's player itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Set playback time
summary: Moves the GUI animation editor's playback to the given time.
details: Vanilla's rewind button passes 0 to go to the start, and the roll forward button passes the animation's end time. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a decimal number, such as '(float)0' or GuiAnimationEditorPlayer.GetMaxDuration

label: Set playing
summary: Starts or stops the animation playback in the editor.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument and returns nothing. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the game does not describe it. Going by the name, it says whether to play.

label: Set loop
summary: Turns looped playback in the editor on or off.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument and returns nothing. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the game does not describe it. Going by the name, it says whether to loop.

label: Set speed multiplier
summary: Sets the playback speed factor of the animation editor.
details: Going by its name. It takes one argument and returns nothing. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the game does not describe it. Going by the name, it is the new speed factor.

label: Pick playback speed
summary: Sets the GUI animation editor's playback speed to the one picked in the speed dropdown.
details: The dropdown calls it when its selection changes and passes the choice itself, so it is written without an argument. It returns nothing.

label: Needle follows keyframes
summary: Whether the time marker (needle) moves along when keyframes are moved.
details: It shows the matching button as pressed, in both the GUI animation editor and the curve editor.

label: Step back
summary: Moves the GUI animation editor's playback one step back.
details: Its button is off while the animation plays. Its tooltip says "Step forward", the same text as the forward button; the step forward button's tooltip says it steps one frame. It returns nothing.

label: Step forward
summary: Moves the GUI animation editor's playback one frame forward.
details: Its button is off while the animation plays. It returns nothing.

label: Play or pause
summary: Starts the animation in the GUI animation editor, or pauses it.
details: Its one use is the play button, which shows a pause picture while the animation plays. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle loop
summary: Switches looped playback in the GUI animation editor on or off.
details: Its one use is the loop button. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle needle follows
summary: Switches whether the time marker (needle) moves along when keyframes are moved.
details: Its button is in both the GUI animation editor and the curve editor, where it also has a keyboard shortcut. It returns nothing.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this speed option entry itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Playback speed text
summary: The text shown for one playback speed in the GUI animation editor's speed dropdown.

label: Multiplier
summary: The speed factor of this playback speed option.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's tooltip files use a `GetMultiplier` on a different type, a static modifier tooltip, so that use says nothing about this one.

label: Self
summary: This speed option entry itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access ruler steps
summary: Gives access to the list of ruler resolution entries of the timeline ruler.
details: Going by its name; what a resolution entry is is not documented. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the timeline ruler itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Ruler mark
summary: The marks of the time ruler above the GUI animation editor's timeline.
details: Its one use draws each mark: main marks with a time label, subdivisions as plain marks. The game does not register its return type.

label: Self
summary: The timeline ruler itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this ruler resolution entry itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Ruler label
summary: The label written at a main mark of the GUI animation editor's time ruler.
details: Subdivision marks have no label.

label: Ruler mark position
summary: Where a mark of the GUI animation editor's time ruler sits, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: It places both main marks and subdivisions.

label: Is subdivision
summary: Whether a mark of the GUI animation editor's time ruler is a minor mark between the main ones.
details: Main marks get a time label; subdivisions are drawn without one.

label: Self
summary: This ruler resolution entry itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Keyframe
summary: The keyframes of a track in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use draws each keyframe's marker on the track's timeline. The game does not register its return type.

label: Track itself
summary: The track itself, to hand to another function.
details: Its one use passes the track to the timeline's BeginDragDuration when its duration handle is pressed. The game does not register its return type.

label: Add keyframe at mouse
summary: Adds a keyframe to this track at the point of the timeline under the mouse.
details: The GUI animation editor calls it on a double-click on the track's timeline. It returns nothing.

label: Clear preview widgets
summary: Removes all widgets that were picked to preview this track's animation.
details: The GUI animation editor calls it on a right-click on the track's preview button, whose tooltip explains this. It returns nothing.

label: Preview widget count
summary: How many widgets are picked to preview this track's animation, as a whole number.
details: The GUI animation editor writes it on the track's preview button.

label: Track name
summary: The name shown for a track in the GUI animation editor.
details: It is the text in the track's left column.

label: Track duration
summary: How long an animation track lasts, as a decimal number.
details: The GUI animation editor writes it at the end of animation tracks. The unit is not shown.

label: Nesting depth
summary: How deeply a track is nested under other tracks in the GUI animation editor, as a whole number.
details: The editor indents the track's name by one step at depth 1 and by two at depth 2 or more.

label: Keyframes
summary: The list of keyframes of this track.
details: Going by its name. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it.

label: Duration handle position
summary: Where the right end of a track's timeline is, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: The GUI animation editor puts the handle for dragging the track's duration there; a comment in the file says it is computed like the timeline's size.

label: Timeline size
summary: The size of a track's timeline area in the GUI animation editor, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: It sizes the right part of the track, where its keyframes are drawn.

label: Has data to animate
summary: Going by its name, whether a track has something that can be keyframed.
details: The GUI animation editor shows the track's previous keyframe, toggle keyframe and next keyframe buttons only while this is true. What counts as data is not shown.

label: Can collapse
summary: Whether a track in the GUI animation editor can be folded shut.
details: Only then does the track show its expand and collapse button.

label: Is collapsed
summary: Whether a track in the GUI animation editor is folded shut.
details: It picks the picture of the track's expand and collapse button.

label: Preview pick mode on
summary: Whether a track is in the mode where clicking a widget picks it to preview the track's animation.
details: The GUI animation editor then shows the track's preview button as pressed and tints it green.

label: Can remove
summary: Whether a track can be removed in the GUI animation editor.
details: Only then does the track show its remove button.

label: Keyframe at current time
summary: Whether the track has a keyframe at the current playback time.
details: It picks the picture of the track's toggle keyframe button, which adds or removes the keyframe at that time.

label: Time within animation
summary: Whether the current playback time lies within the track's animation.
details: It turns on the track's toggle keyframe button, and, while nothing plays, the editing of the track's property.

label: Is animation track
summary: Whether a track in the GUI animation editor is an animation track, the kind that holds the property tracks.
details: Only animation tracks show the preview and add track buttons, their duration and the handle to drag it; they are tinted differently from property tracks.

label: Is property track
summary: Whether a track in the GUI animation editor animates one property of a widget.
details: Only property tracks show the place where the engine puts the property's own editing tools; their remove button has a different picture and their timeline a different tint.

label: Is under mouse
summary: Whether the mouse pointer is over a track's timeline in the GUI animation editor.
details: The timeline is drawn slightly see-through while it is.

label: Next keyframe
summary: Moves the playback time to the track's next keyframe.
details: Its button in the GUI animation editor has this as its tooltip. It returns nothing.

label: Add new track
summary: Opens the dialog for adding a new track to the animation.
details: Its one use is the "+" button on animation tracks in the GUI animation editor. It returns nothing.

label: Previous keyframe
summary: Moves the playback time to the track's previous keyframe.
details: Its button in the GUI animation editor has this as its tooltip. It returns nothing.

label: Remove track
summary: Removes a track from the animation in the GUI animation editor.
details: Its one use is the track's remove button, shown only on tracks that can be removed. It returns nothing.

label: Self
summary: This track itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Toggle collapsed
summary: Folds a track in the GUI animation editor shut, or opens it again.
details: Its one use is the track's expand and collapse button. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle keyframe
summary: Adds a keyframe to the track at the current playback time, or removes the one already there.
details: Its button in the GUI animation editor has this as its tooltip and is on only while the time lies within the animation. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle preview pick mode
summary: Switches on or off the mode where clicking any widget picks it to preview the track's animation.
details: Its button's tooltip in the GUI animation editor says a click on the screen background, or a right-click on the button, deselects all picked widgets. It returns nothing.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the editor's base viewport itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Needle position
summary: Where the time marker (needle) of the GUI animation editor's timeline is drawn, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: Its one use places the needle line and passes the parent widget and two numbers, -1 and 26; what the numbers mean is not shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget the needle is placed in.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A number whose meaning is not documented.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: A number whose meaning is not documented.

label: Self
summary: The editor's base viewport itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the viewport's user input handler itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Selection box position
summary: Where the box dragged with the mouse to select things starts, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: The GUI animation editor and the curve editor place their striped selection box there, measured in the given widget.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget the position is measured in.

label: Selection box size
summary: The size of the box dragged with the mouse to select things, as a pair of decimal numbers.
details: The GUI animation editor and the curve editor size their striped selection box with it.

label: Dragging selection box
summary: Whether a selection box is being dragged with the mouse.
details: The GUI animation editor and the curve editor show their striped selection box only while it is.

label: Self
summary: The viewport's user input handler itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the animation timeline viewport itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Start dragging duration
summary: Starts dragging the end of the given animation track, to change how long it lasts.
details: The GUI animation editor calls it when the duration handle at the end of an animation track is pressed, and passes that track. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The track whose duration is dragged.

label: Can drag duration
summary: Going by its name, whether dragging a track's duration can start now.
details: Its only line is commented out: it would turn the duration handle of an animation track on or off, with a note that this is still to do. The game documents nothing more.

label: Needle position
summary: The position of the time marker (needle) in the timeline viewport, as a pair of numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a pair of decimal numbers and takes three arguments; the game does not name or describe them. No game file uses it.

label: Self
summary: The animation timeline viewport itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this claimant itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on a claimant. In the game's title claimants window, a claimant is someone with a claim on the shown title.

label: Claimant character
summary: The character behind this claimant.
details: The title claimants window sets it as the data context of the box for one claimant, so the widgets inside show that character. The game does not name its return type.

label: Military strength info
summary: The military strength information for this claimant.
details: The title claimants window sets it as the data context of a strength balance widget in the claimant's box. It returns a military strength object.

label: Is ally
summary: Whether this claimant counts as an ally.
details: The title claimants window shows a small icon on the claimant when it is true. The icon's tooltip is headed "Cannot press claim". Whose ally the claimant has to be is not documented.

label: Ally explanation
summary: The text explaining why this claim cannot be pressed.
details: Vanilla places it under the heading "Cannot press claim" in the tooltip of the icon shown for an ally claimant (CLAIMANT_NOT_A_THREAT). Going by its name, the reason is that the claimant is an ally. It returns text.

label: Is implicit claim
summary: Whether this claim is an implicit claim.
details: The title claimants window shows the "implicit claim" label when it is true, and shows the pressed or unpressed claim label only when it is false. What makes a claim implicit is not documented.

label: Is pressed
summary: Whether this claim is pressed.
details: The title claimants window shows the "pressed claim" label when it is true and the "unpressed claim" label when it is false, in both cases only if the claim is not implicit (see IsImplicit).

label: Self
summary: This claimant itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on a claimant.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to the GUI context itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Screen resolution
summary: The screen resolution of the game window, as a pair of numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a pair of decimal numbers, probably width and height. No game file uses it.

label: Self
summary: The GUI context itself, handed on to another data call.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla texts write `.Self` after other objects, such as a character, to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.

label: Access self
summary: Gives access to this council position itself.
details: Going by its name and its use elsewhere: vanilla GUI files write `.AccessSelf` after a widget to pass that object on. The game does not name its return type. No game file uses it on this type.
